# Achalasia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Gastroenterology > Diseases of the esophagus > Achalasia*

[Original Article Link](/library/ug0pC2)

---

## Summary

Achalasia is a condition characterized by impaired relaxation of the <u>lower esophageal sphincter</u> (<u>LES</u>) due to degeneration of inhibitory <u>neurons</u> within the esophageal wall. Symptoms include <u>dysphagia</u> to both solids and liquids (most common), <u>regurgitation</u>, retrosternal <u>pain</u>, and weight loss. <u>High-resolution esophageal manometry</u> is the preferred test to confirm the diagnosis. <u>Upper endoscopy</u> is indicated for all patients to rule out <u>pseudoachalasia</u>, which manifests similarly to achalasia but is caused by another underlying condition (e.g., <u>malignancy</u>). <u>Barium esophagram</u> is often obtained to support the diagnosis and/or assess treatment outcomes in patients with persistent or recurrent symptoms. Definitive treatment options are <u>pneumatic dilation</u>, <u>laparoscopic Heller myotomy</u>, and <u>peroral endoscopic myotomy</u> (<u>POEM</u>); the choice depends on the <u>subtype of achalasia</u>. If definitive treatment is not possible, an injection of <u>botulinum toxin</u> may be used. Medical therapy (e.g., <u>nifedipine</u>) may be considered as a last resort option.

---

## Definitions

* <u>Esophageal motility disorder</u> characterized by inadequate relaxation of the <u>lower esophageal sphincter</u> (<u>LES</u>) and nonperistaltic contractions in the <u>distal</u> two-thirds of the <u>esophagus</u> due to the degeneration of inhibitory <u>neurons</u>

* Etymology: A (absent) -chalasia (relaxation)

---

## Etiology

The cause of achalasia is unknown but may be associated with autoimmune processes, genetic factors, and/or viral infections. [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)

---

## Pathophysiology

* <u>Swallowing</u> is controlled through excitatory (<u>acetylcholine</u>, <u>substance P</u>) and inhibitory (NO, <u>VIP</u>) neurohumoral substances.

* <u>Atrophy</u> of inhibitory <u>neurons</u> in the <u>Auerbach plexus</u> → lack of inhibitory <u>neurotransmitters</u> (e.g., NO, <u>VIP</u>) → inability to relax and increased resting pressure of the <u>LES</u>, as well as dysfunctional <u>peristalsis</u> → esophageal dilation <u>proximal</u> to <u>LES</u>

---

## Clinical features

* <u>Dysphagia</u> to solids and liquids; can be progressive;   or paradoxical dysphagia (difficulty <u>swallowing</u> liquids, while solids are easily swallowed)

* <u>Regurgitation</u>

* Retrosternal <u>pain</u> and cramps

* Weight loss





> [!NOTE]
> Achalasia typically manifests with progressive <u>dysphagia</u> to solids and liquids while esophageal obstruction manifests with <u>dysphagia</u> to solids only.

---

## Diagnosis

### Approach




* Consider achalasia in patients with:

* <u>Clinical features of achalasia</u>

* A suspected <u>diagnosis of GERD</u> unresponsive to <u>PPI</u> treatment [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

* Obtain <u>upper endoscopy</u> to rule out <u>pseudoachalasia</u>.

* Obtain <u>high-resolution esophageal manometry</u> to confirm the diagnosis and classify subtype.

* Consider <u>barium esophagram</u> to confirm the diagnosis if manometry is inconclusive.





### <u>Upper endoscopy</u> [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)[[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)




* Indication: : to rule out <u>pseudoachalasia</u> or other causes of obstruction

* Findings

* Often normal in patients with achalasia

* Suggestive findings include:

* Retained saliva and/or food

* Esophageal dilatation

* Puckered <u>gastroesophageal junction</u> with increased resistance during passage with the endoscope





> [!TIP]
> Perform additional studies including <u>endoscopic ultrasound</u> and <u>biopsy</u> if <u>malignancy</u> is suspected.




### <u>High-resolution esophageal manometry</u> (<u>HRM</u>) [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)[[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)




* Indication: <u>gold standard</u> to confirm achalasia and determine subtype by measuring <u>LES</u> pressure and esophageal <u>peristalsis</u>

* Findings

* Absent or uncoordinated <u>peristalsis</u> in the lower two-thirds of the <u>esophagus</u>

* Impaired <u>LES</u> relaxation (i.e., incomplete or absent) with increased <u>LES</u> resting pressure [[5]](/library/BLdz-q0)

* Possibly increased panesophageal pressure





### <u>Barium esophagram</u> [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)[[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)




Timed <u>barium esophagram</u> (TBE) is preferred if available.  [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)




* Indications

* To support the diagnosis if <u>HRM</u> results are unclear

* To assess treatment outcome in patients with persistent or recurrent symptoms

* Findings

* May be normal

* Suggestive findings include:

* <u>Bird-beak sign</u>: dilatation of the <u>proximal</u> <u>esophagus</u> with stenosis of the <u>gastroesophageal junction</u>

* Delayed barium emptying or barium retention





### Additional studies




* Functional lumen imaging probe (FLIP) [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)[[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)

* Endoscopic tool used to measure esophageal pressure, diameter, and function

* May be used as an additional tool to support diagnosis if results are unclear

* <u>Cross-sectional imaging</u>: for further evaluation if malignant causes of <u>pseudoachalasia</u> are suspected   [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)

* <u>Chest x-ray</u> 

* Not routinely indicated

* May show supportive findings, e.g.: [[6]](/library/Dnd1vq0)

* <u>Widened mediastinum</u>

* <u>Air-fluid level</u> on <u>lateral</u> view

* Possible absence of gastric bubble





> [!TIP]
> Signs of <u>pseudoachalasia</u> include a short duration of < 1 year and <u>significant weight loss</u>. [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)

## Differential diagnoses

### Differential diagnoses of achalasia




* Pseudoachalasia (<u>secondary achalasia</u>) refers to symptoms and/or diagnostic findings (e.g., impaired <u>LES</u> relaxation) that mimic achalasia but are caused by another condition, e.g.:   [[2]](/library/w5dhmq0)

* <u>Esophageal cancer</u> [[7]](/library/jDX_VZ0)

* <u>Gastric cancer</u> and other extraesophageal cancers (symptoms may be due to <u>mass effect</u> or paraneoplasia)

* <u>Chagas disease</u> [[8]](/library/PDXWeZ0)

* <u>Amyloidosis</u> [[9]](/library/4DX3eZ0)

* <u>Neurofibromatosis type I</u> [[10]](/library/kDXmeZ0)

* <u>Sarcoidosis</u> [[11]](/library/ODXIeZ0)

* Extrinsic compression (e.g., <u>mediastinal</u> <u>lymphadenopathy</u>)

* <u>Schatzki ring</u>

* <u>Esophageal stricture</u>

* <u>Scleroderma</u>

* Other <u>esophageal motility disorders</u>





> [!NOTE]
> <u>CHA</u>gas disease may lead to secondary a<u>CHA</u>lasia.




### <u>Esophageal motility disorders</u>




* <u>Esophageal motility disorders</u> include disorders of hypomotility (e.g., achalasia) and hypermotility (e.g., <u>diffuse esophageal spasm</u>). [[12]](/library/uyYpS7)[[13]](/library/Lbbw8H)[[14]](/library/9bbNDH)

* Achalasia is the best described hypomotile esophageal disorder.

* <u>Diffuse esophageal spasm</u> and <u>hypercontractile esophagus</u> are the best described <u>hypermotile esophageal disorders</u>.

* <u>Hypertensive peristalsis</u> (<u>nutcracker esophagus</u>; super-squeeze <u>esophagus</u>)

* Previously considered a <u>hypermotile esophageal disorder</u>; manifests with retrosternal <u>chest pain</u> and <u>dysphagia</u>

* On <u>conventional esophageal manometry</u>, <u>hypertensive peristalsis</u> is characterized by propagative high-amplitude (> 220 mm Hg) esophageal contractions. 
* With the emergence of <u>high-resolution esophageal manometry</u> (<u>HRM</u>), the clinical relevance of <u>hypertensive peristalsis</u> as a diagnosis has been questioned.

* If <u>HRM</u> is not available and symptomatic patients have esophageal <u>peristalsis</u> with an amplitude > 220 mm Hg, treatment is the same as for <u>esophageal hypermotility disorders</u>.

## Treatment

### General principles [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)




* The goal of treatment is to reduce <u>LES</u> pressure to improve symptoms and prevent progression.

* Offer definitive treatment (if feasible) depending on the <u>achalasia subtype</u>.

* Type I or II: Choose any definitive treatment.

* Type III: <u>POEM</u> is preferred.

* Consider pharmacological treatment if definitive treatment options are contraindicated or unsuccessful.

* <u>Esophagectomy</u> may be indicated in end-stage achalasia (e.g., with megaesophagus).





### Definitive treatment [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)




* <u>Pneumatic dilation</u>

* <u>Fluoroscopy</u>- or endoscopy-guided graded balloon dilation of the <u>LES</u> that tears the surrounding muscle fibers

* Indication: type I or II achalasia

* Should only be performed if surgical support is available as there is a 2% risk for <u>esophageal perforation</u> [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

* Laparoscopic Heller myotomy (LHM)

* Surgical procedure in which the <u>LES</u> is <u>incised</u> longitudinally

* Indication: type I or II achalasia

* Often performed with <u>fundoplication</u> to reduce postoperative risk of <u>GERD</u>

* Peroral endoscopic myotomy (<u>POEM</u>)

* Endoscopy-guided myotomy of the inner circular muscle layer of the <u>LES</u> (the longitudinal muscle layer is preserved)

* Indications

* Any achalasia type (preferred definitive treatment for type III) [[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)

* May be considered in other <u>esophageal motility disorders</u> (e.g., <u>diffuse esophageal spasm</u>)





### Pharmacological treatment [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)[[4]](/library/D5d1mq0)




* <u>Botulinum toxin</u> injection

* <u>Botulinum toxin</u> is injected into the <u>LES</u> during endoscopy.

* Indication: any achalasia type in patients who cannot undergo definitive treatment

* Highly effective but temporary  [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

* Oral medication [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

* Least effective treatment

* May be considered if other measures are unsuccessful or contraindicated [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

* Options

* <u>Calcium channel blockers</u>, e.g., <u>nifedipine</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

* <u>Nitrates</u>, e.g., <u>isosorbide dinitrate</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[3]](/library/r5dflq0)

---

## Complications

* Pulmonary complications (e.g., <u>pneumonia</u>, <u>abscess</u>, <u>asthma</u>) caused by <u>aspiration</u>

* Megaesophagus

* Increased risk of <u>esophageal cancer</u>





> [!TIP]
> Although patients with achalasia are at higher risk for <u>esophageal cancer</u>, routine <u>cancer screening</u> is not recommended.




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
